messages.subject: Problems with model convergence when adding SNPs
messages.subject_clean: Problems with model convergence when adding SNPs
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I was wondering if anyone has been through a similar situation and could give me some advice. I'm currently working on a two-factor model with 8 traits (N for each trait: 132395; 132667; 133517; 132132; 132559; 120430; 122886; 975353).

Model fit is not great at first:

model = 'F1 =~ TRAIT1 + TRAIT2 + TRAIT3
                F2 =~ TRAIT4 + TRAIT5 + TRAIT6 + TRAIT7 + TRAIT8
                F1~~F2'
$modelfit
      chisq df       p_chisq      AIC       CFI      SRMR
df 1049.495 19 1.429052e-210 1083.495 0.8246252 0.1206166

But, after removing one trait (highly correlated with another one) and adding a constraint for one of the traits, model fit improves:

model = 'F1 =~ TRAIT1 + TRAIT2 + TRAIT3
                F2 =~ TRAIT4 + TRAIT5 + TRAIT6 + TRAIT7
                F1~~F2
                TRAIT1 ~~ a*TRAIT1
                a > .001'
$modelfit
      chisq df      p_chisq      AIC       CFI       SRMR
df 135.0242  8 2.566287e-25 161.0242 0.9581731 0.06285507

However, when adding the SNPs to run the GWAS I start facing some problems. I'm running the model with unit loading identification so that I can estimate the N_hat afterwards (for computing polygenic scores). I get a lot of warnings (for most SNPs honestly) that some lv residual variances are negative. I noticed that this is mainly about the residual variance of factor 1, so I tried constraining its residual variance to be positive just to see if it would change anything in the results, but then the model doesn't converge for most SNPs.

I have done a lot of troubleshooting these days. I have tried removing certain traits to keep the model simpler but nothing seems to help. So, I decided to check how the GWAS would run while using unit variance identification. To my surprise, the GWAS runs smoothly with no warnings.

I know that I cannot simply use the results from the GWAS with unit variance identification as I would underestimate the N_hat. So, I'm a bit lost as I have tried all I could think of and nothing seems to work and I cannot just ignore and remove the SNPs with warning as they are almost all of my SNPs.

Best,
Dener

messages.subject: GWAS-by-subtraction amount of variance
messages.body_plain:
Hi GenomicSEM-team,

I am interested in using the GWAS-by-subtraction application of genomicSEM but have a few questions.

1. In your paper, Demange et al., 2021, you report "The NonCog  latent  factor  accounted  for  57%  of  total  genetic   variance  in  educational  attainment". Where from did you derive 57%? Did you square the unstandardized estimate?

2. The GWAS-by-subtraction results include both standardized and unstandardized estimates. In your paper, you report the unstandardized estimates, while standardized estimates are more commonly reported in other applications of genomicSEM (in my understanding). What is the rationale for reporting unstandardized estimates here?

Thanks in advance!
Jet

messages.subject: Negative heritability warning
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm trying to reproduce the results for User Specified Models with SNP Effects. I found the round 1 Neale Lab UK Biobank GWAS results are not available now, so I tried the round 2 Neale Lab UK Biobank GWAS results.

When I run the ldsc function, there is a warning:
In ldsc(traits = traits, sample.prev = sample.prev, population.prev = population.prev, : Your genetic covariance matrix includes traits estimated to have a negative heritability.

And when I run the userGWAS function, there is an error:
Error in { : task 1 failed - "system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 4.57139e-17"

I think according to the definition of SNP heritability it should be positive?  I wonder if anyone else has encountered this issue and has some tips for that?

Thanks for your help.

Best,

Kylie

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I encountered the same issue with models that were working previously and now produce the same error and no output. When running a model with DWLS estimation that has no convergence problems, the warning message for emptystand is NULL rather than 0 so it seems to fail the check on line 710.

I was able to do a quick fix by adjusting the code on lines 481-483 of usermodel.R from

      if (estimation == "DWLS") {
        emptystand <- .tryCatch.W.E(Fit_stand <- sem(Model1,
                                                     sample.cov = S_Stand, estimator = "DWLS", WLS.V = W_stand,
                                                     std.lv <http://std.lv> = std.lv <http://std.lv>, sample.nobs = 2, optim.dx.tol = +Inf))
      }

to

      if (estimation == "DWLS") {
        emptystand <- .tryCatch.W.E(Fit_stand <- sem(Model1,
                                                     sample.cov = S_Stand, estimator = "DWLS", WLS.V = W_stand,
                                                     std.lv <http://std.lv> = std.lv <http://std.lv>, sample.nobs = 2, optim.dx.tol = +Inf))
        if (is.null(emptystand$warning$message[1])) {
          emptystand$warning$message[1] <- 0
        }
      }

But I think this is a bug that needs to be fixed because there were otherwise no issues with the model solution.

messages.subject: Re: Negative heritability warning
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

since LDSC estimates heritability as the slope of a regression of the Z2 on the LD score, that slope can become negative. This cna happen with sumstats derived from certain tpes of mixed modesl (not likely the case here) or for low powered GWAS (so low N or low N_cases)/

Hope this helps!

Michel

Hi there,

We are using Genomic SEM to run a multivariate GWAS on a five factor model identified via EFA. In preparing summary stats, using the reference panel provided on the gSEM GitHub, we are continuing to get the error:
"Error in { :
  task 1 failed - "Non-numeric argument to mathematical function"

When we run traceback() to see where the non-numeric argument is being applied to mathematical function, we get:
2: stopifnot(is.list(x), identical(quote, "auto") || isTRUEorFALSE(quote),
       is.character(sep) && length(sep) == 1L && nchar(sep) == 1L,
       is.character(sep2) && length(sep2) == 3L && nchar(sep2[2L]) ==
           1L, is.character(dec) && length(dec) == 1L && nchar(dec) ==
           1L, dec != sep, is.character(eol) && length(eol) == 1L,
       length(qmethod) == 1L && qmethod %chin% c("double", "escape"),
       length(compress) == 1L && compress %chin% c("auto", "none",
           "gzip"), isTRUEorFALSE(col.names), isTRUEorFALSE(append),
       isTRUEorFALSE(row.names), isTRUEorFALSE(verbose), isTRUEorFALSE(showProgress),

Any ideas about how to identify where and what needs to be changed in our code?

Thank you for your help,

Shannon

messages.subject: Re: "Starting GWAS Estimation"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dominic,

A single run of all SNPs could take 24 hours depending on the complexity of the model and the number of SNPs being analyzed. See this post on the google group for some things to consider:
https://groups.google.com/g/genomic-sem-users/c/ZJtXg56fQsg/m/1XHglsX9BAAJ

Ideally you would want to both run in parallel and use an array or driver script to submit multiple jobs that are running in parallel.

Best,
  Andrew
